- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.22) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 5 days at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.11) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation; add 2–5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 3–7% downward bias for long-term forecasts.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for each negative sentiment day following the turn.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 1.5x moving average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days ago, model tends to overreact; apply 3–5% downward correction to forecast for next 7 days.
